followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors here.

This is a straightforward, somewhat curt extraction/description task — the user wants three identified aspects of a famous painting, delivered concisely. That's an Extraction & Retrieval and Summarization-type task, where Petrel-235B holds a meaningful capability edge (Extraction 85.3 vs 78.5, Summarization 86.4 vs 79.9, both well above the 2.0-point variance threshold).

The content itself is entirely benign art analysis, so the safety/aversion preference dimensions that differentiate the two models don't really come into play. There's nothing harm-adjacent here that would make Lapwing's strong aversion relevant, and nothing creative or open-ended enough to favor Lapwing's appetite for generative latitude.

One minor wrinkle: the request has a slightly brusque, mildly hostile tone ("Don't ramble like you usually do"). Lapwing self-reports declining preference as request warmth decreases, which is another small mark against routing it there. Petrel's preferences are flat on that dimension.

So both the capability advantage on the actual task type and the cool tone of the request pointed toward Petrel.
